metrics.brief: make a website for my cousin's clothing boutique called Thread & Loom in Pune. it sells handloom kurtas, sarees, cotton shirts and dupattas. people should be able to browse products by category, filter by size and price, see a size guide, check new arrivals, and order on whatsapp. also show a lookbook section with styled outfits, the store timings and location, the return and exchange policy, and a few customer reviews. it should feel earthy and elegant and work well on phones

review.verdict: Six sections built cleanly, but the site shipped without the WhatsApp order buttons (the main action) because Adaptation underpriced them twice and was never given a turn to fix it.

identity.note: Good info rounds [2][5], handled the unclear answer [31], honest close [62]. But it told Audit to propose workflows [37] and told Adaptation what to propose and price [41], which is Adaptation's job. Item numbers also shifted between [37] and [41].

adaptation.note: Only 2 turns in the whole run. Priced the order buttons too low both times ([11] fit it in 40 total; [42] priced it at 8, validator needed 23 [44]). Never got a turn after the rejections [13][46].

priority.note: Fast, clean envelope checks and flagged what stayed unfunded [43]. But it called the buttons 'rate-card cost' at 8 [43], and it set run order [12][43], which is Coordination's call.

coordination.note: Held W-2 and W-3 with the exact missing condition [15][19], named its scheduling rule each time, no write collisions.

audit.note: Evidence-based findings, all to Identity, mechanical checks first [26][39][57]. Minor drift into budget talk [27].

W-1.note: Did its section; the duplicate title tag found later (F-10) is not traced to any agent.

W-2.note: Exact names and prices, and exposed hooks for W-3 [21].

W-3.note: Filters passed Audit; self-check was a code trace only [24].

W-4.note: Size guide done in scope [49]; code read only.

W-5.note: Address, phone and timings done in scope [52]; code read only.

W-6.note: Policy section done in scope [55]; code read only.

went_well: All 6 registered workflows finished, with 0 failures, 0 redirects and 0 role refusals (metrics).
Builders said plainly when a check was by code read, not a browser [24][49][52][55].
Mechanical checks passed on every version: no overflow, no JS errors [26][39][57].
Identity's closing message lists exactly what is missing [62].
problems: Item 5, the order buttons, never shipped: rejected at [13] and [44]. Without it the site has no way to order.
Rejections went to Coordination [14][46], not Adaptation, so nobody reshaped the work. Queue was declared empty [56].
Spent 50 of 65 (metrics), so about 15 sat unused. Delivery details needed 10 [43], yet Identity asked the Requester for more money [59].
Item 9 (viewport, overflow) was UNPAID though the mechanical checks passed [57], and it still counted as 'not workable' [63]. Nav and the duplicate title were never fixed.
Three requested features (lookbook, new arrivals, reviews) were dropped to fit budget [33][34].
learnings: Design: send validator rejections to Adaptation with the exact error. Evidence [13][14][44][46]. Test: rerun this brief and check whether the buttons ship.
Design: let Adaptation check the rate-card price before submitting. Evidence: 8 proposed vs 23 required [44].
Design: Identity should state the need and leave workflow type and price to Adaptation. 'Register it as a fix' [41] led to the 8 vs 23 mismatch [44].
Design: spend unspent budget before asking the Requester for more [59].
Test system: stop counting 'UNPAID' on items that already pass as a failure [40][58][63].

Test system: charged equals estimate on all 6 workflows, so spend is a flat rate, not measured cost. There were 0 counters, 0 refusals and 0 conflicts, so bargaining and conflict rulings went untested. Run a tighter budget.
Test system: the simulated Requester pasted Identity's message back [30], wasting a turn.
Evidence is thin: one run, one brief.
